summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka, and later taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed his studies at the University of Oxford in 1963. He served at Monash University (~1965–2004) and as Professor at Aichi Bunkyo University in 2000.

Ian Reader (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate from the University of Leeds in 1983. He held posts at Lancaster University (~2000–2006) and the University of Manchester as Emeritus Professor (~2006).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar (2001–2007) studying under Farid Khan, Taj Ali, and Ihsan Ali. He served as Professor and Chairman at Peshawar in 2001 and later at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (b. 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later held posts there from around 1967 to 2006, as well as at Otani University Junior College.

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita, later teaching at Tohoku University (~1952–1965) and serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (b. 1942), an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Komazawa University under Kogen Mizuno and at Otani University. He served as associate professor (1975) and professor (1985–2013) at Komazawa University.

Ichiro Numata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University under Jitsuzo Kuwabara from ~1922 to 1925 and later held a post at Kyoto University from ~1936 to 1965.
Ida Vassalini (1891–1953) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Padua and the University of Milan, where she also held a teaching post.

Ignatij Andreevich Kossovich (1808–1878) was a linguist who studied at Vilnius University and Saint Petersburg State University. He served as Professor of Greek at Polotsk Uniate Theological Seminary (1833–1835) and at the University of Warsaw (1872–1878).
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at Sapienza University of Rome and later served as a professor there from 1876 to 1919.

Ignác Goldziher (1850–1921) was a religious studies scholar who studied under Ármin Vámbéry, Emil Rödiger, and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer at Budapest, Berlin, and Leipzig. He was a professor at Eötvös Loránd University from 1872.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1944–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1960–1998).

Igor Dmitrievič Serebrjakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He taught at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1941–1947) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961).

Igor Mikhailovich Reisner (1898–1958) was an Indology and history scholar educated at the Frunze Military Academy. He held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from ~1950 to 1958.

Ihsan Ali (b. 1955) is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Peshawar and UCL under Frank Raymond Allchin. He has served as a professor at Peshawar and as Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).

Ikko Arai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Komazawa University. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa (b. 1968) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he was attested as a lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2017, she was attested as a special researcher at Otani University and an affiliated researcher at Kyoto University.
